To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a brief tailored psychological intervention, delivered by health professionals trained to provide it and supported by clinical supervision, was effective in reducing distress in patients with cancer, and was feasible and acceptable for patients and health professionals.

a tailored psychosocial intervention delivered by health professionals who undergo focused training in the delivery of psychosocial care and participate in clinical supervisions is feasible and effective in reducing anxiety and depression in people with cancer.

A brief tailored psychosocia l Intervention for patients with Cancer delivered by health professionals who have undergone brief training and clinical supervision is feasible and acceptable to patients and health professionals, and has potential to improve patient outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a model of care for cancer patients that is designed to improve patient outcomes and reduce distress and burden for health professionals.

the development and testing of an integrated model of psychosocial care for patients with cancer that will improve the delivery of psychosocial interventions in the cancer context, and improve the quality of life of patients with cancer.

the identification of factors that may influence the development of psychological distress in patients with cancer, and the evaluation of a model of psychosocial care that may reduce distress and improve patient outcomes.

the study will provide important data on the effectiveness of brief, targeted psychosocial intervention in routine care and will identify enablers of and barriers to its implementation in routine clinical practice.
the PROMPT intervention has a significant effect on reducing anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients with cancer.
the study is a randomised trial of psychosocial intervention in cancer patients integrated into clinical practice.

we have developed an innovative, evidence-based psychosocial intervention, PROMPT (promoting optimal outco mes in mood through tailored psycho-social therapies) that is designed to be integrated into the routine cancer care pathway.

the intervention was well tolerated by patients and health professionals, and was associated with improvements in anxiety, depression, unmet needs, and health professional stress.
